title: Variant parity healthcheck and update plan for tokenizer/context/tooling
creator: Jordan Lee
description:
Context:
The smart routing system can route requests across regions, customer tiers, and fallback model variants. To keep fallbacks safe and predictable, we must ensure tokenizer parity, context-window behavior, and tooling interfaces (function-calling, structured output, streaming) are compatible between primary models and their fallback variants. Past incidents showed subtle tokenizer differences causing broken tool calls and increased hallucination when we fell back during capacity pressure.

Goal:
Establish an automated, reproducible maintenance plan that (1) runs daily parity healthchecks across all model pairs used in smart routing fallbacks, (2) surfaces actionable diffs for tokenizer and context behavior, (3) gates fallback promotion via CI/rollout checks, and (4) integrates parity signals into the Console and routing policy heuristics.

Scope (what this ticket owns):
- Define the parity checks (tokenization alignment, context truncation/overflow behaviour, special tokens, tool-calling schema compatibility, streaming and chunking semantics).
- Implement a CI job that runs the parity suite for each primary->fallback variant mapping nightly and on PRs that touch model packaging or tokenizer code.
- Add a lightweight canonical prompt corpus (100 seed prompts across workloads) for deterministic comparison and a non-deterministic quality spot-check harness (10k randomized prompts) for statistical drift detection.
- Create a parity scoreboard per mapping: tokenization delta, avg response divergence, functional-tool-call pass rate, and contextual-length equivalence.
- Provide remediation playbooks (quantization-adjusted tokenizers, pre-normalization hooks, micro-translation layer) when parity fails.
- Wire key parity alarms into Console and routing layer so policies can prefer parity-safe fallbacks first.

Out of scope:
- Large-scale model re-training.
- Full model-level evals unrelated to tokenizer/context/tooling parity (those are separate eval initiatives).

Success metrics:
- Nightly parity run coverage >= 95% of active fallback mappings.
- Mean tokenization delta per mapping < 0.5% for top-10 customer prompts.
- Tool-calling regression rate < 0.1% after rollouts that changed fallback mappings.
- Automated gating prevents at least one risky fallback promotion during the next release window.

Acceptance criteria:
- Parity test suite merged and green in CI for the runtime-2.4 branch.
- Nightly runner deployed to infra with reporting to the Console parity dashboard.
- A remediation playbook and on-call runbook documented in Confluence and linked from the parity dashboard.
- Routing policy code can query the parity scoreboard API and prefer fallbacks marked "parity-safe".

Deliverables / milestones:
1) Definition doc + canonical prompt corpus (contrib: Research, Applied ML) — due 2026-03-04.
2) Parity test harness + CI integration (contrib: Runtime/Infra) — due 2026-03-14.
3) Nightly runner + dashboard surface (contrib: Console) — due 2026-03-21.
4) Remediation playbooks + routing integration (contrib: Runtime/Platform) — due 2026-03-28.

Implementation notes and proposed approach:
- Tokenizer parity uses byte-level hashing of token sequences and a normalized token mapping to account for benign differences (e.g., BOS/EOS placement). We store sample token sequences for each seed prompt and compare Hamming and edit-distance metrics.
- Context window behavior is tested by synthetic chains that expand until truncation; we assert that truncation points map to semantically equivalent prefixes and that KV cache behavior preserves tool-calls across continuation boundaries.
- For tooling and function-calling parity, we run the same canonical function schema against both variants and validate call structure, arg types, and return codes. Failures are categorized by schema mismatch vs. behavioral mismatch.
- The CI job will be parameterized to run quick checks on PRs and full checks nightly. Quick checks use the 100-seed corpus; nightly runs include probabilistic sampling of 10k prompts spread across customers and contexts.
- Where tokenizer differences are unavoidable (e.g., bespoke tokenizers for quantized variants), we maintain micro-converters (thin normalization layers) and treat them as first-class remediation steps; these converters must be versioned with the model variant and tested by the parity suite.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Nightly runner is heavy and increases infra cost. Mitigation: throttled sampling and prioritized mappings (customer-impact high mappings run at higher frequency).
- Risk: False positives from non-deterministic models. Mitigation: seed determinism for parity tests where possible; statistical thresholds for accept/reject rather than binary checks.
- Risk: Routing integration causes routing latency. Mitigation: parity scoreboard cached in Console with TTL; routing layer pulls only mapping-safe boolean flag during decision time.

Notes for rollout with Smart Routing policies:
- Routing policy tiering should prefer fallback variants annotated as "parity-safe" for a given primary; for mappings without parity data, treat as "unknown" and use conservative fallback thresholds.
- Region-selection policies: ensure nightly parity checks include regionalized variants (GPU/quantization differences by region) so that fallbacks selected by region are evaluated in-region when possible.
